In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of efficiently transferring large quantities of data from a processor to an external logic analyzer.
the development of efficient techniques to reduce the time required to transfer cache contents off-chips, and to save the expensive logic analyzer memory during post-silicon debugging.
the design and implementation of an effective compression strategy for processor debug.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed technique results in a 7-31%, and 54% reduction respectively, in the transfer time and the amount of memory used on the logic analyzer.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an efficient compression scheme for processor debug support that results in 7 to 54% reduction of the transfer time and 7 to 31% reduction of the storage requirement.
we present a compression strategy for cache contents that results in a significant compression ratio improvement, and a parallel compression architecture to further reduce the off-chip transfer time.

we have developed a compression engine that exploits the knowledge about the data being compressed, and a parallel architecture that can compress the data in parallel, resulting in faster transfer time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cache aware strategy is a simple and effective way to improve compression of cache data.
the compression engine needs to be aware of cache structure to achieve better compression.
the cache aware compression technique can be easily implemented in hardware with a small silicon overhead and can result in significant reduction in debug time.
